claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me start with a few questions.

**First, could you tell me the name and age of the child or children you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Alex is 17 years old, which is helpful to know.

Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to understand the rules better. Let me check the official guidance to ensure I'm giving you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. I've reviewed the eligibility rules. Now I have a few more questions about Alex to determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he attending school, college, university, or an approved training programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and isn't studying anything right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

Based on the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I need to inform you of the situation regarding Alex:

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training. However, since Alex is 17 and is **not** currently in approved education or training, he would not qualify for Child Benefit.

The rules do allow for a 20-week extension period if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, without knowing whether Alex has registered with one of these services, he may not meet the eligibility criteria.

**To give you a complete picture: has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving school?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with anything like that. He just left school and hasn't signed up with the careers service or armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to make a determination about your eligibility.

Based on the information you've provided and the Child Benefit eligibility rules:

- Alex is 17 years old
- He is not currently in approved education or training
- He has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

According to the eligibility rules, you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex. The rules state that you normally qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training. While there is a 20-week extension available if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a careers service or the armed services, Alex has not done this.

Without either being in approved education/training or having registered with one of the qualifying services, Alex does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

However, I'd recommend contacting HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly if you'd like to discuss your specific circumstances further, as there may be other considerations I'm not aware of.
